why: phase-417 W4.e -- the Rust half of the one creation shape (`NodeCtx::create_guard_condition`), and the verb a Rust user writes. rclrs has no counterpart: it builds a `GuardCondition` from a `Context` and hands it to a wait set (rclrs's wait-set machinery; the reason is stated in full at `cpp:WaitSet`), so there is nothing for this to correspond to -- which is what makes it an extension rather than a rename. It returns `(HandleId, GuardCondition)`: the id is the arena slot, for `trigger_one` and `bind_handle_to_sched_context`, and the handle is what goes to the other thread. Node-level BECAUSE it binds the node: the guard takes the node's default `SchedContext`, which is the whole content of "the node owns it" for a callback sharing one executor with every other tier in the image (RFC-0047). The ours-only primitive underneath is `rust:Executor::register_guard_condition`.
